subtopic: Token Holder Rights vs. Underlying Shareholder Rights
source_evidence: Under this model, the price of the tokenized security changes with the price of the referenced security, but the investor has no claims or rights against the issuer of the referenced security.
answer: A token’s price tracking a company’s stock does not necessarily mean the token holder has the rights of a shareholder in that company. With a synthetic tokenized security, the investor has no claims or rights against the issuer of the referenced security, and the token holder’s rights and benefits may differ significantly from those of an underlying shareholder. So, distinguish price exposure from shareholder rights.
